mission: Ben begins at Shedu Maad in a state of quiet disconnection: respected, loved, and included, but not at ease among peers or ordinary Jedi social life. Luke and close family are temporarily offworld, leaving Ben not abandoned but alone when the past reaches him. Add living Shedu Maad texture: training rooms, shared meals, Hapan architecture and security formality rubbing against Jedi informality. Include a brief light Allana/Amelia cameo or near-cameo while she is visiting for the week - ordinary family texture only, not plot machinery. Ben is included in ordinary banter, but the room turns careful around him once his history is remembered. The obsolete GAG identity-address alert arrives and unsettles him before the content does. He recognizes the channel as a dead part of his old GAG service marker routed through standard HoloNet infrastructure, not Jedi comms. His hand covers the sender code before he realizes he is hiding it.
why_now: Chapter 2 occupies the setup phase and carries the next locked outline turn.
conflict: Ben should feel young, defensive, lonely without being self-pitying, and secretly hungry for meaningful work. Shedu Maad should show that he has care but little ease. The message scares him because it comes from old GAG history, but it also gives him an unwanted sense of purpose: perhaps the part of his past everyone avoids can help him do something good.
turning_point: Ben holo-calls Luke before leaving for Coruscant.
closing_hook: Ben holo-calls Luke before leaving for Coruscant.
setting: Shedu Maad (Hapes Cluster), Jedi Order headquarters complex. Mid-morning training salle, refectory tables, and Ben's quarters. Hapan architecture: high windows, cool stone, formal protocol overlaid on Jedi informality. Allana Solo (under her 'Amelia' identity) is visiting that week; warm but guarded family-life texture. Ben moves through public spaces respected but not at ease. The obsolete GAG identity-address alert arrives on a private holocomm in his quarters.
emotional_trajectory: Ben should feel young, defensive, lonely without being self-pitying, and secretly hungry for meaningful work. Shedu Maad should show that he has care but little ease. The message scares him because it comes from old GAG history, but it also gives him an unwanted sense of purpose: perhaps the part of his past everyone avoids can help him do something good.
